what_happened: A job meant to make the steward "step back" and decide for itself landed. Afterward the person running Athena saw that the steward is still limited to the two lowest ladder rungs (defaults and conventions). Anything above that (design, budgets, role changes) is now recorded without asking anyone, so nobody acts on it. The steward's "step back" is also still only a look across repeated failures, not a fresh read of Athena's own design or instructions. The person running Athena reported it instead of fixing it by hand. This is a correction of landed output, not a rejected job, so no criteria or checks are listed.
cause: A request about what the steward should do was read as a change to its prompt or behavior wording. Nothing made the reading trace the governing rule, the ladder limit in the roles-and-ladder design doc, that caps what the role may act on. Nothing checked that the requested behavior could take effect once the job landed. The same ladder rule had already blocked an earlier request, and the reading step still does not look for rules that would stop an agent from acting on a new instruction.
prevention: When a request changes what a role should decide or do, the reading step must list the rules that bound that role's actions (ladder rungs, budgets, role limits) and put any blocking rule into scope as a deliverable. Where a rule is owner-governed, the reading must name the question for the owner instead of leaving it out. The criteria must check the behavior: given an item above the lowest two rungs, the steward acts on it or escalates it with a stated question. They must also check that the step back reads Athena's design and instructions, not only repeated failures.
proposed_request: Make the steward able to act on what it finds when it steps back. Outcome: the steward does a fresh read of Athena's own design and instructions on a regular cadence, not only after repeated failures. Where it finds a problem above the defaults and conventions rungs (design, budgets, role changes), it either makes the change or queues it as a job with a clear decision question for the owner. It does not just record it. Amend the ladder rule in docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md and the matching decision entry so this is allowed. Keep the owner reserved for environment changes and token spend, which are the only things the owner wants to hear about. Acceptance: a test with a recorded item above the second rung shows the steward acting on it or queuing it with a question. A test shows the step back reads the design docs and prompts, not only the failure records. The ladder doc and decision record agree with the new behavior. Add a changelog entry.
